races.name: Cleansing Service Group Novice Stakes (gbb Race)
British Ebf Peter Willett Future Stayers' Maiden Stakes (Sire And Dam Restricted Race) (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
Royal Sussex Regiment Ebf Fillies' Conditions Stakes (gbb Race)

runners_data.name: Al Samsama
runners_data.note: Unbeaten in one start at Goodwood over 6f on similar going, now stepping to 7f under Ryan Moore for Richard Hughes, who is in sharp 3/27 T14 form; the natural pacesetter here and holds the class edge in this field, but how the duel with The Can Can Queen plays out is the central tactical question.
runners_data.comment: Al Samsama won on her most recent outing and has run over today's trip, making her a lively danger off stall two carrying 132 lb; the fitness question after 53 days off is the one factor to weigh against her.

runners_data.name: China In Your Hand
runners_data.note: Three Goodwood runs including a win at this course and distance, giving strong track form, but her naturally prominent style has been pushed to a rear mapping because the field is loaded with pace — she is unlikely to get the handy position she needs, which tempers her chance in race shapes that depend on that berth.
runners_data.comment: Rated well below the pick of these on our figures and ranked last of the six runners, China In Your Hand faces a stiff task despite winning two starts back and drawing stall one, though she has experience over today's trip and arrives on a reasonable freshness of 31 days.

runners_data.name: Sorrengail
runners_data.note: Charlie Appleby's progressive filly steps up from 6f to 7f for the first time wearing a hood, with William Buick retaining the ride; has won and placed at Goodwood already this season, travels prominently, and the step up in trip looks likely to suit given her two-length winning margin last time.
runners_data.comment: Landed a win two starts back and chased home the winner last time out, giving her a solid profile heading into this; she has run over today's trip and at 132 lb from stall six, Sorrengail looks the one to beat, her rating of 84 heading the field.

runners_data.name: Spirit Tango
runners_data.note: Won over 6f at Sandown on her most recent start, making it two runs in and showing clear improvement; Ralph Beckett's yard is in strong form (T14: 8/41) and Oisin Murphy's booking is significant, though 62 days off and the Goodwood track-form question remain things to weigh.
runners_data.comment: Spirit Tango arrives here on the back of a win last time out and has run over today's trip, with draw four a neutral factor at 132 lb; the main risk is the 62-day absence leaving questions over peak fitness.

runners_data.name: The Can Can Queen
runners_data.note: Front-runner by nature and will contest the early lead hard, but recent form is inconsistent — a win at Goodwood over 6f back in her history is her best, yet the 2024 string shows 5-1-5-3-0-7 including two defeats at this track; Callum Shepherd rides and she may set the pace without lasting home over 7f.

runners_data.name: Global Success
runners_data.note: A multiple placer at 6f who is now tackling 7f in blinkers for the first time; naturally a prominent racer but pushed into a midfield mapping because there is no room at the front in this field, meaning she is unlikely to secure a position that suits her rhythm, and a 13-day turnaround is brisk at this level.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Global Success has shown some ability — a second two starts back and a third five starts back — but finishing fifth last time out does little to inspire confidence, and our rating has her fifth of six in the field.

races.paceDynamic: Al Samsama and The Can Can Queen are both confirmed front-runners, meaning this 7f Goodwood conditions race will be genuinely contested from the off, with neither likely to yield the lead without a fight. That early duel sets up an honest, pressured gallop across the rising Goodwood terrain, which will almost certainly string the field out and put a premium on finishing power rather than sheer pace. Sorrengail, Spirit Tango, and China In Your Hand are all prominent types who will be pressing just behind, meaning the race has significant pace depth across the first three or four positions. This shape strongly favours a horse with the class and stamina to travel prominently and sustain their effort through the final two furlongs — a quality prominent racer who can hold a good position without burning energy in the early battle will be best placed. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate cleanly; Al Samsama and The Can Can Queen are best placed to actually secure their natural positions, with Sorrengail the likeliest to lock in directly behind them, while China In Your Hand and Global Success are unlikely to enjoy the forward berths their styles naturally demand.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Stayer Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If Al Samsama and The Can Can Queen push each other through a strong early pace, softening both and handing the race to the horse best able to sustain into the Goodwood dip and rise.
scenarios.body: The pressured front-running duel drains the leaders, and the horse travelling most efficiently in the prominent-to-midfield range finds an energy reserve to power home; this scenario rewards class, a strong 7f stamina profile, and a rider who can switch off early.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Controls, Quickens Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Al Samsama dictates matters uncontested after The Can Can Queen fails to match strides early, establishing a fluent, controlled gallop.
scenarios.body: A single front-runner setting an honest but measured pace can dictate terms and prove very hard to peg back at Goodwood, where the undulations suit a horse who travels within itself; Ryan Moore's ability to manage energy makes this outcome viable even from a contested starting point.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners go excessively hard early and tie each other up, creating a truly strong gallop that produces a sprint finish from behind.
scenarios.body: A strongly-run race occasionally hands the race to those who were shielded from the pressure, but this scenario is undermined here because the horses nominally mapped further back are true prominent types pushed rearward, not genuine hold-up specialists with tactical finishing pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Crawl, Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the two front-runners surprisingly ease back under pressure from their jockeys and the race devolves into a falsely-run crawl before a sprint home.
scenarios.body: A slow early pace would compress the field and create a lottery sprint over the final two furlongs, neutralising Al Samsama's class advantage and bringing lower-rated runners into contention; however this is unlikely given both leaders have confirmed front-running profiles and strong handlers pushing them forward.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Al Samsama or The Can Can Queen gives ground early — if neither concedes, the duel will be fierce and both could be vulnerable to a prominent chaser from the second rank.

Sorrengail's first run at 7f is a key unknown; if the extra furlong beyond her previous trips reveals a stamina limit, the race could tilt sharply toward horses with more proven staying power at the trip.

Global Success wears blinkers for the first time over a new trip — if headgear sparks a brighter early effort, she could force her way into contention rather than settling into midfield, changing the pace dynamics above.

Goodwood's undulating 7f track historically punishes horses who expend energy early on the uphill section; the front-runner battle makes this terrain factor especially relevant today and worth monitoring as the field passes the halfway point.

China In Your Hand's Goodwood record (1 win, 2 places in 3 starts at the track) is strong, but her redistribution to a rearward position means punters should note she may not get the forward pitch that has underpinned those course runs.

races.name: Virgin Bet A Good Bet Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Jax Edge
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner here and the race-shaper; his Goodwood form includes a win over 6f and a recent second over 5f at this course, and with no pace rival to challenge him he can control tempo — his style fit score of 0.94 reflects that he operates best when able to lead freely, which is exactly what he gets today.|
runners_data.comment: Jax Edge ran a fine second last time out and has experience of both today's trip and going, so conditions hold no surprises; carrying 137 lb from stall two, the weight burden is the one factor that could just blunt her finishing effort.

runners_data.name: U S S Charleston
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up type who has placed at 5f on good ground at Goodwood (2nd/5f/GOO in recent history), but his wider similar-going record (5/15) is modest and he needs a stronger pace than Jax Edge is likely to set to deliver his best from off the bridle.|
runners_data.comment: Placed third last time out and second three starts back, U S S Charleston brings solid recent form into this, and his experience over today's trip and going on a quick 17-day turnaround makes him a genuine threat; the main concern is a winless run of six starts in recent form.

runners_data.name: Spring Bloom
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old prominent racer with outstanding Goodwood course form — four of her last five runs are at this track over 6f in good ground, recording two wins and multiple placings; stepping back to 5f is untested recently but her prominent, pressing style gives her every chance to capitalise if Jax Edge weakens.|
runners_data.comment: Spring Bloom arrives on the back of back-to-back wins three and four starts back, and his experience over today's trip and going holds him in good stead at a workable weight of 133 lb; the worry is that two consecutive unplaced efforts since those victories leave him needing to find his best again.

runners_data.name: Nogo's Dream
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore in the saddle is always a notable booking, and this hold-up horse has solid 5f Goodwood form (2nd/5f/GOO twice), but a Good surface over five furlongs without a truly testing pace is not his ideal recipe — he needs something to chase down.|
runners_data.comment: Nogo's Dream arrives here in good shape just 15 days after his last outing, and his experience over today's trip and going is a clear asset; second two starts back gives him a solid recent placed effort to point to, and an 81 rating topping the field marks him as the one to beat despite being winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Independent Expert
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up specialist whose natural station is at the rear of the field; his recent form string (568946) reflects struggles to land a blow, his similar-going record at this distance is limited (5/15, 0W0P), and being pushed forward from his true rearward position reduces rather than enhances his chance.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Independent Expert nevertheless showed some encouragement with a fourth two runs back, and she has experience of today's distance and going; carrying 132 lb from stall four, she looks a midfield contender at best.

runners_data.name: Over Spiced
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy takes over on this mare who has a genuinely strong 5f Goodwood profile (2nd, 3rd, 3rd in her last three at this course); though a natural hold-up type nudged forward in the map, her repeated placed efforts at this exact venue suggest she is better placed than her style redistribution might imply — headgear noted.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked bottom of this field on our figures, Over Spiced faces a stiff task despite the fitness edge of an 11-day turnaround and experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Kiss And Run
runners_data.note: Prominent racer from the Rachel Cook/John Bridger yard with a consistent placed record at 5f on good ground at Goodwood (3rd/5f/GOO twice in five runs); OR 66 makes her the lowest-rated prominent horse in the race but her tactical position and track affinity keep her relevant.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Kiss And Run faces a stiff task from a rating of 66, and though she has run over today's trip and going and returns on a fresh enough 11-day break, her recent form — latest a third, but fifths and lower before that — makes her hard to fancy at the foot of our rankings.

races.paceDynamic: Jax Edge is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner sprint and, with no genuine rival to press him from the gates, he is set to dictate a measured, sustainable gallop from the Goodwood five-furlong chute. Spring Bloom and Kiss And Run will push forward to contest prominent positions, creating a competitive early order without turning it into a cavalry charge, which means the fractions should be honest but not suicidal. The true hold-up types — Nogo's Dream and U S S Charleston — will be given ground to make up from the rear, while Independent Expert and Over Spiced, both natural hold-up horses, are redistributed into the midfield map because the field cannot physically accommodate four closers at the back; their effective position will sit closer to midfield than they would ideally prefer, blunting their late-run threat. This race shape — a controlled, uncontested lead, good ground, and a short five-furlong trip — tilts clearly in favour of prominent racers who can settle just off the pace and produce a sustained finish, rather than true hold-up horses needing a searching tempo to do their best work.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Jax Edge Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Jax Edge breaks well and sets an uncontested, rhythm-based gallop that suits the prominent brigade.
scenarios.body: Jax Edge dictates from the front and, without a pace rival to unsettle him, runs to his own rhythm through the dip and up the rise, making it genuinely difficult for hold-up horses to generate momentum over just five furlongs on good ground. Spring Bloom, with her strong Goodwood form and prominent style, is perfectly positioned to chase and overhaul if Jax Edge flattens out, while Kiss And Run similarly benefits from sitting just off the pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Hold Sustained
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fast enough to string the field out but Spring Bloom or Kiss And Run track optimally and finish strongest.
scenarios.body: A genuine early gallop from Jax Edge combined with a prominent tracking position from Spring Bloom or Kiss And Run means those two can exploit any late fade from the leader without needing the race to truly fall apart. Spring Bloom's course-and-distance winning profile and trainer form (2/19 over 14 days) make her the most likely beneficiary of this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final furlong and genuine closers find an unusual amount of daylight to run through.
scenarios.body: Nogo's Dream and U S S Charleston would need Jax Edge to go too fast early and tie up badly for their hold-up style to pay off over this sharp five furlongs on good ground, which is not the projected shape. Even if the pace does collapse, Independent Expert and Over Spiced — both redistributed from their natural rearward position — are unlikely to be sitting far enough back to produce the sweeping late finish this scenario demands.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Drama
scenarios.trigger: If Jax Edge misjudges the gallop and goes far too fast, causing a field-wide reshuffle in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: In the unlikely event that Jax Edge burns up the first two furlongs and leaves the field chasing a ghost, a horse like Over Spiced — who despite redistribution at least carries strong 5f Goodwood course form (2/5f/GOO, 3/5f/GOO) — could be the beneficiary if she manages to hold a better position than her natural style implies. This scenario is low probability precisely because Jax Edge is flagged as a sustainable pacer and there is no rival to force him into a speed duel.

watchPoints.text: Watch Jax Edge's early sections — if he is allowed to bowl along unchallenged and sets a comfortable pace, prominent racers Spring Bloom and Kiss And Run are the most dangerous immediate pursuers and a tactical duel between those three over the final two furlongs is the most likely race shape.

Spring Bloom is stepping back from 6f to 5f on a course where all five of her recent runs have been over the longer trip — monitor whether the shorter distance blunts her finishing kick, particularly up the Goodwood rise.

Independent Expert and Over Spiced are both genuine hold-up types shown in midfield positions they may not naturally secure; if they drift back to their true station the race may be over for them before they find clear running on this five-furlong track.

Ryan Moore on Nogo's Dream demands respect given his three wins from 27 rides for the trainer over 14 days, but the projected pace scenario — controlled and uncontested — is exactly the kind of race shape that can leave a hold-up horse like Nogo's Dream with insufficient petrol to chase down.|

Over Spiced ran just 11 days ago and has multiple recent efforts over this exact course and distance; watch for any market support as Oisin Murphy's booking on a horse with strong 5f Goodwood place form is notable even accounting for her hold-up redistribution.

races.name: Virgin Bet Handicap Stakes (gbbplus Race)

runners_data.name: Manxman
runners_data.note: Won over 1m4f at Goodwood last time out and has solid course form; William Buick's booking is a significant positive, and the prominent style suits a steady-tempo 2m race perfectly — he is one of the horses most likely to secure an early handy position ahead of Bahadur.|
runners_data.comment: Third two starts back reads well on profile, and he has run over today's trip and going before; at 139 lb the weight is a question, but 20 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh and fit enough to outrun his recent figures.

runners_data.name: Synergism
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's operation is in strong current form (8/25 over 14 days) and Synergism's stamina at 2m has been proven with a win over 1m4f at Goodwood; 46 days off the track is worth noting but Prescott runners typically arrive ready, and a prominent style suits this race shape well.|
runners_data.comment: Synergism won three starts back and was third two starts back, showing he knows how to perform at this level, and with his trainer firing at 32% in the past fortnight he arrives in good hands; the question is whether 46 days off has left him short of peak sharpness.

runners_data.name: Bahadur
runners_data.note: Runs in headgear and holds natural front-running/prominent instincts, but with Manxman and Synergism also wanting to be handy, he is likely to be pushed back from his preferred position; his Goodwood and longer-trip form has been inconsistent (9th, 7th here recently), and the style-fit discount is real.|
runners_data.comment: Bahadur steps up as the top-rated runner in the field and his experience over today's trip and going is a clear asset, but his recent sequence of deteriorating finishes — ninth last time out — is the one concern connections must answer.

runners_data.name: Fireblade
runners_data.note: Saffie Osborne takes the ride for Dylan Cunha and Fireblade needs a stronger pace than Sax Appeal is likely to set to generate any meaningful late momentum; a 14th at Goodwood on similar going on the recent sim-going record is a stark flag, and the hold-up profile is the least favoured in this tactical race.|
runners_data.comment: Fireblade shaped with real promise when third and second in consecutive starts, and our rating of 95 puts him comfortably ahead of his official mark; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 20 days since his last run leaves him fresh. The risk is that he has been winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Sax Appeal
runners_data.note: Lone confirmed front-runner who gets a soft lead with no one to press him; Charlie Johnston's yard has been active (2/34 over 14 days) but Sax Appeal's recent form shows a string of thirds without ever winning, and being caught late by a prominent horse tracking him is his chief danger.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Sax Appeal has been a model of consistency in third yet rarely threatens to go one better, and ranked last of five on our figures he faces a stiff ask here; the 65-day absence adds an extra question mark, though he has run over today's trip and going before.

races.paceDynamic: Sax Appeal is the sole confirmed front-runner in this five-runner field and, with no genuine rival to press him, should be allowed to dictate a measured, controlled tempo over the two-mile trip on good ground at Goodwood. Manxman and Synergism are both prominent types who will likely sit just off the leader, creating a compact early order and leaving Fireblade to track from the rear in his customary hold-up role. With only one horse setting the pace and the race expected to be run at a steady, sustainable gallop, the race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can travel close to the pace and pick off a tiring front-runner in the straight, rather than hold-up horses needing a truly strong pace to generate momentum. The field contains more prominent types than can all occupy their natural position — Bahadur is a genuine prominent racer who has been mapped to midfield, and Manxman and Synergism are more likely to secure the early handy positions ahead of him.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sax Appeal Controls Tempo
scenarios.trigger: If Sax Appeal is allowed to bowl along unchallenged at a steady gallop, stretching the field into a line through Goodwood's undulations.
scenarios.body: Sax Appeal sets his own rhythm without pressure and may simply prove difficult to reel in late if the pace is modest enough to leave him fresh; prominent horses Manxman and Synergism are ideally placed to track and challenge but must quicken from close range.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely steady and Manxman or Synergism travel smoothly before asserting in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A controlled gallop suits horses who can travel in a rhythm close to the pace and produce a sustained effort down the Goodwood straight; Manxman's course-winning form at this track and distance makes him particularly well-placed for this outcome.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse — Closer Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the early tempo is so slow that the race turns into a sprint finish and Fireblade, tracking from the rear, finds the others stopping in front of her.
scenarios.body: A falsely slow race can occasionally produce a sprint finish on the run-in, allowing a horse with a strong late kick to pick up the pieces; Fireblade has shown a clear preference for coming from off the pace and would be the primary beneficiary if the leaders tie each other up.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Bahadur Defies Redistribution
scenarios.trigger: If Bahadur manages to secure a prominent position early and produces the sort of front-running or handy-tracking display that is his natural game.
scenarios.body: Bahadur is racing out of role as mapped and his form figures at Goodwood and Sandown over this sort of trip have been patchy, making this a lower-probability outcome; only if Manxman and Synergism miss the break or are ridden conservatively does he get his preferred berth.

watchPoints.text: Sax Appeal's unchallenged lead is the defining tactical factor — if he bowls into the straight with a length or two in hand and plenty left, the prominent horses may have left themselves too much to do.

Manxman and Synergism will both want to sit in second or third — watch the first half-mile to see which of them, or whether Bahadur, actually secures the handy position, as this could significantly alter the race dynamic.
Bahadur's redistribution to midfield means he may be caught in no-man's land — neither tracking the pace nor able to come from behind — which would effectively remove him from contention early.

Fireblade's hold-up profile is extremely dependent on pace, and with only five runners and one front-runner, a truly searching gallop is unlikely — monitor whether she is given a positive ride or left too far back on the final turn.

The going is confirmed Good at Goodwood for this race, with no significant variation across the card — no horse has a material going advantage or concern, so draw and going can be set aside as differentiating factors.

races.name: Virgin Bet Supports Safe Gambling Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Oasis Sunrise
runners_data.note: Strong course-and-distance profile (three placed efforts over 1m2f at Goodwood), prominent style suits a controlled-pace race perfectly, Cieren Fallon a key booking, carries 142lbs but consistent sim-going record of 12/15 backs confidence here.
runners_data.comment: Oasis Sunrise showed a placed effort two starts back and has experience of today's trip and going, but her ninth last time out is a concern, and 142 lb is a stiff burden for a filly rated 70 stepping back in quickly on 11 days' rest.

runners_data.name: Sir Edward Lear
runners_data.note: George Wood takes the mount on a horse who has finished fourth twice over this course and trip; prominent runner who handles Good ground and travels well in the group, though inconsistency and a recent soft-ground run are minor concerns.
runners_data.comment: Sir Edward Lear has run over today's distance and going before and is experienced at the trip on a rating of 72 with conditions to suit, but he remains winless in his last five starts and that elusive first win is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Hello Cotai
runners_data.note: True hold-up runner who has won twice over 1m on Good ground at Goodwood, suggesting real track affinity; Jim Boyle barn in form (T14: 1/15) and Pat Cosgrave knows his way around here, though the 1m2f trip is on the outer edge of comfort.
runners_data.comment: Hello Cotai won last time out and is fit on an 8-day turnaround, with experience of today's trip and going in his favour, but two wins in his last six starts alongside a ranking of ninth of twelve on our figures makes him hard to fancy at this level carrying 142 lb.

runners_data.name: Blue Wonder
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy's presence elevates interest considerably after an 87-day break — last run produced a soft-ground win, and this Good surface is different, though his Goodwood fifth over 1m suggests track familiarity; genuine hold-up type who needs a proper gallop to deliver.
runners_data.comment: Blue Wonder won two starts back and has experience of today's trip and going in her favour, making the 87-day absence the main query; carrying 140 lb from stall nine, she looks capable of going well if retaining that winning form.

runners_data.name: Boy George
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner and keystone of the entire race shape; three Goodwood wins over this course and trip are outstanding credentials, but 441 days off is a significant fitness risk that could unravel the pace he controls — Dominic Ffrench Davis has had just 0 winners from 7 in the last 14 days.
runners_data.comment: A lengthy absence of 441 days is the principal concern with Boy George, who is ranked near the foot of our assessments despite an official mark of 65, and that layoff makes his excellent recent winning sequence — three wins in his last four starts — very hard to assess at face value.

runners_data.name: Lady McC
runners_data.note: Poor recent form, 131-day absence, and a going concern flag (tongue-tie); manages only two sim-going placed efforts from six attempts and has never threatened at this class or trip — Paddy Bradley faces a tough task.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and off the track for 131 days, Lady McC faces a fitness query on her return, though she has run over today's distance and going and a our rating of 70 offers mild encouragement from stall five at 137 lb.

runners_data.name: Decalogue
runners_data.note: Jamie Osborne's three-year-old has been stepping up in trip after a season at 7-8f and ran respectably (second, third) in similar company recently; Saffie Osborne rides for her father, ran just five days ago which could be a concern, but the yard is in sharp form (T14: 4/16).
runners_data.comment: Decalogue has been knocking persistently on the door, finishing second last time out and third two starts back, and his rating of 72 gives him a live chance here; the main risk is that he is returning just five days after his latest effort.

runners_data.name: Prodigal Son
runners_data.note: Heather Main's four-year-old is a natural sit-and-wait type placed at the rear in most recent runs, but with so many hold-up horses in this field he is unlikely to get the clean run from the back that he needs; Luke Morris is an able partner but the tactical squeeze at the rear is a real obstacle to his chance.
runners_data.comment: Ranked tenth of twelve on our figures, Prodigal Son faces a stiff ask, his form patchy in recent starts with a ninth two runs back undermining an encouraging second last time out; he has run over today's trip and going before, and a draw of two is his one neutral positive.

runners_data.name: Connie Moon
runners_data.note: Wears a visor and has been beaten off a low base in similar contests; the horse's instinct is to race well off the pace, yet the crowded hold-up end of this field means she will be fighting for a position she cannot naturally secure — Denis Coakley's record suggests this is a tough ask.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Connie Moon has at least run over today's trip and going before, and 29 days between runs suggests she arrives fresh, though a career-best effort is needed from stall seven off 134 lb to trouble the principals.

runners_data.name: Platinum Prince
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old veteran in a blinkers, shown one-pace finishing ability at similar trips for Gary & Josh Moore (T14: 3/29, showing the yard is active); his natural rear-running style is compromised by the same midfield congestion affecting other hold-up types, and at OR 61 the weight of evidence points away.
runners_data.comment: Platinum Prince has run over today's trip and going before, but has been winless in his last five starts, finishing no better than fourth in recent outings; carrying 133 lb from stall 12, there is enough encouragement to suggest a bold showing, though a win looks elusive.

runners_data.name: Benavente
runners_data.note: Finley Marsh partners a horse whose form is puzzling — a 7f Stamford win from a current 1m2f Goodwood assignment is a big ask; only one sim-going run from fifteen attempts is alarming, and stepping from sprinting to a mile-and-a-quarter feels opportunistic.
runners_data.comment: Benavente landed a winning blow two starts back and shaped with promise when third four starts back, bringing strong claims off a top-ranked our rating of 74; the question is whether he can bounce back from an unplaced effort last time.

runners_data.name: Brave Leader
runners_data.note: Tom Ward's three-year-old has course experience (ninth over 1m2f at Goodwood) and David Probert is an upgrade; a natural hold-up type who, unlike some others in this end of the field, has the youth and trip-building arc to get involved — yet no wins from seven runs and a crowded final furlong remain stubborn concerns.
runners_data.comment: Brave Leader has been winless in his last five starts, with a best recent finish of fourth, and ranked last on our figures he faces a stiff ask here; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 12 days since his last outing suggests he is at least fit.

races.paceDynamic: Boy George is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner field and, returning from 441 days off, faces a critical fitness question — yet his recent Goodwood form (three wins at the track including back-to-back 1m2f victories) suggests he knows how to dominate here. With no genuine pace rival to press him, he can dictate at a controlled, sustainable gallop that keeps the race together and reduces the winning margin, favouring those who can travel prominently and produce an organised finish-line kick rather than a sweeping late run. Oasis Sunrise and Sir Edward Lear are the likeliest prominent horses to benefit from a tucked-in, uneventful trip, while the hold-up contingent — crowded out at the back — must hope for a strong pace that never materialises. The race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can sit just off the leader and pounce inside the final two furlongs, as a lone front-runner dictating a fair pace on Good ground at Goodwood is tailor-made for those travelling in his slipstream. Prodigal Son, Connie Moon, Platinum Prince, and Brave Leader are all genuine hold-up horses who have been pushed into midfield on the map because the field holds more true sit-and-wait types than can all get to the rear; of those four, Brave Leader (David Probert, course experience) is best placed to obtain a workable position, but all four will face a stiffer task than the map position implies.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Boy George Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Boy George settles in front, controls his own fractions, and the hold-up horses are left with insufficient pace to peel off the back.
scenarios.body: Boy George finds his old rhythm on a course where he won three times, setting a fair gallop that suits prominent-tracking types who can accelerate in the final quarter-mile; the lack of pressure keeps the pace honest rather than fast, leaving late-closers stranded.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is moderate and two or three prominent horses race within a length of the leader throughout, producing a bunched finish at the two-pole.
scenarios.body: Oasis Sunrise and Sir Edward Lear, both proven on this course and distance, exploit a clean passage from prominent positions to overhaul a tiring Boy George close home; Good ground suits both and neither needs a strong pace to travel.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Gets Gap
scenarios.trigger: If Boy George sets a stronger-than-expected gallop on return from his layoff and genuine closers find daylight earlier than usual.
scenarios.body: A faster-than-anticipated early pace causes the field to string out, giving a hold-up runner a clear sight of rivals two furlongs out; Blue Wonder (Oisin Murphy, capable of winning off a break) or Hello Cotai, whose Goodwood 1m win shows sharp course form, could fill the gap.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse and Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Boy George's fitness fails after his 441-day absence and the gallop drops sharply mid-race, causing a falsely-run scramble.
scenarios.body: Without a reliable pace-setter, the race becomes a sprint from the two-furlong pole and positional advantage becomes paramount; the closest-tracking prominent horses inherit the race by default in a messy finish.

watchPoints.text: Boy George's fitness after 441 days off is the single biggest variable in this race — if he labours or fades before the straight, the entire pace dynamic collapses and a falsely-run scramble replaces the controlled scenario the field expects.

Oasis Sunrise has placed three times over 1m2f at Goodwood without winning — watch whether Cieren Fallon commits earlier than usual or waits for a gap that may not come if Boy George slows the pace to a crawl.

Blue Wonder (87-day break, Oisin Murphy) could be sharper than his layoff suggests — if he produces his soft-ground winning form on this Good surface, he represents a significant value threat to the headline prominent types.

The redistribution of Prodigal Son, Connie Moon, Platinum Prince, and Brave Leader into midfield means the real rear of the field is effectively empty — watch whether any of them drift back to their true position early, which could cause crowding and interference in the middle stages.

Decalogue ran only five days ago; if fitness or freshness is an issue Jamie Osborne may instruct Saffie to ride conservatively early, which could leave the yard's runner in no-man's land between the prominent group and the stacked midfield.

races.name: Virgin Bet Daily Price Boosts Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Mister Bluebird
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who can dictate unchallenged here; wears headgear (hg:p), last ran 10 days ago in good order, but course-and-distance form shows a string of places without winning and his OR of 84 leaves little room for error at the head of affairs.
runners_data.comment: Mister Bluebird has back-to-back seconds in recent starts and our rating of 88 marks him as a genuine threat to the top-rated runner, with the return to today's trip and going a clear positive at a quick ten-day turnaround; the risk is that he has been winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Marengo Storm
runners_data.note: Three-year-old in good form — won twice at six furlongs including at Goodwood, trainer Hughes in 3/27 over 14 days; prominent style fits this pace map perfectly and course familiarity is a concrete asset in what should be an orderly race.
runners_data.comment: Marengo Storm won two starts back and has run over today's trip, but fifth last time out after 38 days off gives pause, and 137 lb is a stern burden for a gelding who has looked inconsistent in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Old Is Gold
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy takes over for Balding, a powerful combination; wears visor, all recent runs have been at Goodwood which is a major plus, though last five starts are over five furlongs and the step back to six here needs to be assessed carefully against what is a modest field.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Old Is Gold nonetheless posted a third five starts back and arrives fit on 20 days' rest, with experience of today's distance and going; our rating of 92 makes him the one to beat off 136 lb from stall 8.

runners_data.name: Atticum
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner from Robert Cowell's yard who has placed four times without winning in similar going; last ran 41 days ago which is a notable gap, and his deeper-running style means he needs the pace to be strong enough to set up a late surge on a track that doesn't always reward closers.
runners_data.comment: Atticum shaped with plenty of promise when third last time out, and a winner five starts back, with experience over today's trip and going working in his favour. The main risk is a 41-day absence, though he arrives carrying 136 lb from stall three and the rating of 88 suggests he retains serious claims.

runners_data.name: Arry Up
runners_data.note: Front-foot three-year-old who has won twice this season; last ran 13 days ago, prominent style means he will sit close to Mister Bluebird early and could prove a nuisance if he gets a good tow into the race, though his Goodwood record shows a 19th-place finish here already.
runners_data.comment: Arry Up was beaten into sixth last time out and ranks eighth of nine on our figures, making him hard to fancy under 135 lb; the positives are a winning effort two starts back and experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Brosay
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a modest recent record — five finishes of 6th or worse in the last five runs; wears blinkers (hg:b), trainer Pike has 0 from 7 over 14 days, and the form figures at Goodwood specifically are uninspiring, making this a speculative hold-up play at best.
runners_data.comment: Brosay has run over today's distance and going, arrives here on a fresh 27-day break, and our rating of 87 suggests he holds more ability than his official mark of 80 implies — yet winless in his last six starts, consistency remains the concern.

runners_data.name: An Outlaw's Grace
runners_data.note: Hannon runner with place form in similar going who naturally wants to come from off the pace; however, with Evie Ross also needing the rear, this runner has been mapped to midfield rather than its natural deepest position — that compromise slightly blunts its late-running effectiveness and warrants a discount accordingly.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked seventh of nine on our figures, An Outlaw's Grace faces a stiff task, and a trainer operating at just four per cent in the past fortnight does little to inspire confidence; the return to today's trip and going at least offers some familiarity.

runners_data.name: Born Slippy
runners_data.note: Last ran 41 days ago and wears tongue-tie; a single win this season came on Soft ground and the only Goodwood run produced a 25th-place finish, making it hard to identify a clear route to competitive involvement from its hold-up position.
runners_data.comment: Third three starts back offers some encouragement, and he has run over today's trip and going before, but two unplaced efforts since then — the most recent 41 days ago — leave fitness and consistency as questions he must answer from stall 6 off 130 lb.

runners_data.name: Evie Ross
runners_data.note: Cox-trained three-year-old who wears a visor and consistently finishes mid-pack at around 5th–6th; a true hold-up runner by nature, she has been placed into a midfield mapping position due to field congestion at the rear, which means she is unlikely to get the deep cover and late surge that her style demands — factor in an OR of 72 against mostly higher-rated rivals.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked bottom of this field on our figures, Evie Ross faces a stiff ask, though she has run over today's trip and going before and returns after a reasonable 21-day break from stall two carrying 125 lb.

races.paceDynamic: Mister Bluebird is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to press him for the lead, he should be able to control tempo from the front on Good ground over six furlongs at Goodwood — a track where a solo pace-setter can dictate comfortably into the straight. Marengo Storm, Old Is Gold, and Arry Up will push forward to chase him, creating an organised mid-pack cluster that leaves the race shape clear and relatively steady in the early stages. The field holds more hold-up types than can authentically settle at the rear — An Outlaw's Grace and Evie Ross are genuine come-from-behind runners that the map has redistributed to midfield, meaning their natural late run will be compressed and their effectiveness discounted. This shape favours horses racing prominently just off the leader, able to pounce when Mister Bluebird's effort flattens in the final furlong — the prominent-to-midfield profile with course form and tactical awareness is the primary beneficiary.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Solo Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Mister Bluebird sets a measured, uncontested pace and the prominent duo Marengo Storm or Old Is Gold track and strike turning in.
scenarios.body: Mister Bluebird controls a sensible gallop without being harried, leaving the race perfectly set up for those racing on his quarters to quicken off the bend; Goodwood's undulating straight rewards horses who travel smoothly at the head of affairs and produce a strong sustained burst.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Benefit
scenarios.trigger: If Mister Bluebird sets an unusually slow tempo and the race becomes a sprint finish, allowing midfield horses to close the gap easily.
scenarios.body: A crawl in the early stages would compress the field significantly and turn this into a dash from the two-furlong pole, nullifying Mister Bluebird's positional advantage; Atticum and An Outlaw's Grace, though the latter is racing out of his natural deepest hold-up role, have the tactical speed to benefit if the field bunches.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Genuine Hold-Ups Fire Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is honest enough to stretch the field and genuine late runners can pick up strongly through the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Brosay or Born Slippy would need the pace to be truly testing to make up enough ground from the rear at Goodwood, where the straight is demanding but not excessive at six furlongs; this scenario is constrained because An Outlaw's Grace and Evie Ross — the field's most natural closers — are both redistributed and unlikely to secure ideal cover.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Gallops Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Mister Bluebird produces a career-best front-running display and the chasing pack misjudges how much to give him.
scenarios.body: With eight rivals crowding forward or mid-pack, any tactical confusion in behind could allow Mister Bluebird to steal an unassailable advantage into the Goodwood straight; he has placed twice over this course and distance and carries headgear, giving him a small but real chance if the prominent horses over-commit chasing.

watchPoints.text: Marengo Storm has won twice at Goodwood over six furlongs and races prominently — watch for him to slot in directly behind Mister Bluebird and produce the decisive mid-race move that this pace shape sets up.

Mister Bluebird's inability to win from the front in recent starts (0 wins from 4 places in similar going) raises the question of whether he will be caught in the final furlong; watch for prominent challengers sweeping past him inside the final 150 yards.

Arry Up has shown front-forward tendencies and a win at five furlongs this season — watch whether he pushes Mister Bluebird hard enough early to disrupt the controlled tempo the pace map assumes, which would alter the entire race shape.

An Outlaw's Grace and Evie Ross both need deep-field cover to produce their best; if the early pace is slow and the field compresses, watch whether either can manufacture a meaningful run from their compressed midfield positions rather than a true hold-up berth.

Old Is Gold has run exclusively over five furlongs recently and is now stepped back to six — watch in the final furlong whether stamina holds as Goodwood's run-in tests finishing reserves more than a flat straight would.
